sections.text: Arjuna replied: My Lord! O Immutable One! My delusion has fled. By Thy Grace, O Changeless One, the light has dawned. My doubts are gone, and I stand before Thee ready to do Thy will.
Sanjaya said: Thus have I heard this rare, wonderful and soul-stirring discourse of the Lord Shri Krishna and the great-souled Arjuna.
Through the blessing of the sage Vyasa, I listened to this secret and noble science from the lips of its Master, the Lord Shri Krishna.

So we had been discussing chapter 18, Moksa Sannyasa Yoga. Yoga of Liberation through renunciation. Liberating yourself from all that is binding you.
What is binding me is my limitations. Im limiting myself by associating with my body, mind and intellectual. So in the end, Bhagavan Samara says, sarva Dharma Parityajya Maam Ekam Sharanam Praja.
Give up your dependence on your body, mind and intellect as the source of your happiness. That eternal happiness which you are seeking, you are right now dependent on your body, mind and intellect. Ill gain through my power, Ill gain through my intellect.
Ill gain through my manipulating the others. Bhagavan said, give up all those and just take refuge in me, the source, the self, the consciousness. And I will take care of all your sins.
All the things which you have as negative impressions, I will take care of. I will wipe them out and make you clean so that you can experience the joy which is your nature. This is praptasya pravtvi.
This is something which we already have. All we have to do is clear that which is veiling that happiness. So we concluded the discourse on Bhagavad Gita.
Bhagavan also said who you should not be teaching this knowledge to. One who does not have any discipline. One who does not have any devotion towards this knowledge.
One who has no sense of service to others -- in other words, someone so self-centered. Such a person will not be able to learn anything from you because hes so self-centered. Then lastly he said, the one who cavils at this knowledge or at me -- if I do not have any faith in any idea, I will never be able to learn.
In Gujarati, when a child is crying for a long time, they say Asu ragda tyanay -- Ragada means raga tana, pulling. Why are you pulling all these ragas? You know why they said that? There was a kind of contempt against the people who perform classical music and go on and on. So when somebody has no appreciation for classical music, they associate it with babies crying: Why are you doing ragada? Thats cavilling towards that art -- having no respect for it. Sometimes, you know, people go for a dance program and say, So how was it? The same old South Indian dancing all the time. Because they were looking for Bollywood dancing, and it turned out to be a Kathak classical dancing concert.
Because they have no appreciation for the art. I have seen the Ghatapata -- the discourse about Vedanta where they use the analogy of the pot. Ghata Pata, Ghatapada -- in Bombay they say Garbhad Karta, right? Ghatapata became Gadbar. No appreciation for that discussion or discourse.
Now such a person -- if you try to teach him the same thing, one who says Garbhad -- you try to teach him Vedanta, it will not work. One who says Vairu Ragda, he will not learn music. He has no appreciation for it.
So Bhagavan says such a person, you should not be teaching this Bhagavad Gita. He has to come to a level where he has disciplined himself. He has devotion for this knowledge and he has a sense of service.
In essence, he does not think about his own good but sees oneness with others. Thats how we do service. We can only serve somebody whom we revere, appreciate, or love.
For one who has none of this for this knowledge, you should not be teaching that to him. On the other hand, Bhagavan said, if you have learned this knowledge -- by Gods grace you got this chance to learn this precious knowledge from your teacher -- you should share it with others. Do not be self-centered.
If youre a Christian who comes and asks me, thats fine. You dont just become a scholar; share this with others. This is the concept of franchising, right? You have a concept and give it to others.
Thats how it grows into a huge multinational. Otherwise selling burger, how can that be a big business? It is the simplest thing in the world. Take a bun and put a patty in between.
Put little lettuce, tomato and ketchup, youre done. But its a multinational entity. Because the concept of franchising.
Somebody asked Einstein, is there anything baffles you in this world? He said, the concept of compound interest. Somebody demonstrated to me: if you get one penny the first day, then it doubles the next day, and you keep doubling pennies -- versus I give you a million dollars right away -- which one in 20 years will be greater? He demonstrates that the doubling pennies will be worth millions of dollars. The compound interest.
So compounding this knowledge for the greater good of society -- it is every students duty to share this with others. Those who are interested and are worthy. So therefore Bhagavan said, such a person will certainly will come to me now.
Teaching this subject which you have learnt, you become master at it. After a while you become one with that subject. If you learn music, then continue teaching music.
You will become a master of it. Because you are practicing more and more and more by every time you teach to somebody else. So Bhagavan says, such a person will certainly come to me.
He will become me in a sense he will attain that oneness he is seeking with his own supreme self. So Bhagavan is actively asking you to go out and teach others. How does one become a Jagat Guru? By introducing the idea of the study group.
If he had just said come to my lecture, we would have gone to his lectures and left. I did that for a long time. I met when I was 17 years old.
First I just went to his lectures, because in India I did not know about study groups. When I came to the USA, the first series I attended in 1983, I had no idea about study groups. But end of the Gita Yajna that those of you who are interested must now attend a study group.
And I said, What is a study group? So Gaurang Nanavati from Houston called me up because I had filled out that form. I had no interest really in joining a study group, because I was thinking, Who else other than a great master can teach me this? But because it, I had that little Shraddha -- I must go. And thats how I went to a study group.
This is where I started truly learning Bhagavad Gita, not from s lectures. So the idea of these study groups has made Chinmaya Mission a great organization in sharing this knowledge. The idea came from Bhagavan Sri Krishna: share your knowledge.
Bhagavan said, such a person will certainly achieve the goal hes seeking. Then he said, there is no one in this world who is closer to me than the one who is teaching this Bhagavad Gita with Shraddha, with having supreme faith in me, in this knowledge. You cannot teach something if you are not convinced about it.
You can only convince others. If you are convinced about it with conviction. One who teaches this Bhagavad Gita, Bhagavan says, I dont think theres anyone who is dearer to me, anyone who is nearer to me than that person.
Because he came closest to the goal of becoming one with that universal self. So Bhagavan has glorified the teachers and the teachings. And then he said, Adhyeshyate Cha Imam Dharmyam Samvadam Avayoho Gnana Yagnena Tena Aham Ishtaha Syam Iti Me Matihi.
Now the student -- is there anything beneficial in just learning? One who studies this dialogue of ours about Dharma. This dialogue, Bhagavad Gita, all 18 chapters of it -- this is a dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna. So Krishna is telling Arjuna: this, our dialogue about Dharma.
What is right, what is wrong, what is real, what is unreal. Who studies such a person? I consider that such a person is worshipping me through Gnani Yajna. He may not be a Krishna Bhakta.
He may not be doing Sri Krishna, Shranham, Sri Krishna, Shrana, Sri Krishna. He may not be going to the temple at all. He may not bow down at Krishnas statue in the temple.
But Bhagavan said -- it is not that I will consider or not consider -- it is my conviction that such a person is worshipping me through Gnana Yajna. So the student who is studying Bhagavad Gita, Bhagavan said, is directly worshipping me. And we have learnt in Bhagavad Gita previously: how do you serve your teacher? By living the ideal the teacher teaches is the best service to your teacher.
Your teacher teaches you music and you dont do anything about it. But just keep giving him fees and never learned music. Is that a service to him? It may make his living.
But he is not very proud of you. But my teacher teaches me something and I excel in it. And then propagate that knowledge even further.
He will be very proud when he hears about you. Even today, if you go and tell Gaurangbhai that you went to Neelkants class -- you know why? He is my teacher. When he hears that, he knows that after all these years, Neelkant is still into Bhagavad Gita, has not given up.
Thats a service to your teacher. So Bhagavan said, such a person, Ill consider that hes serving me directly. Hes worshipping me directly through Gnana Yoga word Yajna Signifies sacrificial fire is invoked and devotees are offering oblations in it.
You see here, the fire of knowledge is kindled by your studies and you are offering your ignorance into it. Up till now what I considered me and now no, it is not me. So my ignorance about myself, which in common language we call ego is what we are offering into this Gnar Yajna.
Therefore, Bhagavan said, I am convinced, Im convicted that such a person is worshipping me through Gnan Yajna. So the student is glorified here. Then the next verse says, okay, but what about somebody who is not even studying? We have heard this before -- there is a difference between reading and studying.
Ed: you read a newspaper. You really have no other interest but to get some information whats going on? So you are reading newspaper, but you study your subject. I have to study because I want to know the knowledge.
So not just reading Bhagavad Gita. So just chanting Bhagavad Gita may or may not do much good to you. But studying Bhagavad Gita, Bhagavan said, Im convinced that you are worshipping me through Gnani Yajna.
But what if Im not studying? Shraddha Vaan Anasuyash Cha Shrunuyat Api Yo Naraha. A person who is listening to this knowledge -- he may not be studying intently, he may not be reading Bhagavad Gita. But hes listening to the discourse about Bhagavad Gita, about the knowledge of Bhagavad Gita from a Sadguru.
But you have to have faith in it. Youre not just listening to find out what it is all about. With Shraddha -- when we listen to somebody like the Dalai Lama or Sri Sri Ravi Shankar or somebody in whom we have Shraddha -- we are intently listening to what hes saying.
Were trying to understand the message behind it. Thats Shraddha Vaan Anasuya. Hes not listening to find out what is wrong in it.
As we had heard before, Max Muller and those scholars were given grants by European powers to go and study Sanskrit -- to find out what all this garbage was that they were teaching their people, and then tell them that it was all wrong. Thats Anasuya -- cavilling at that knowledge. But if you are not doing it for that reason -- and it turns out that Max Muller became probably the greatest scholar because he probably had the real intention, even though his sponsors may not have -- then such a person who is just listening to this discourse about Bhagavad Gita, the knowledge of Bhagavad Gita, So Api Muktaha -- he also will get liberated.

Verse 73 is Arjunas triumphant response: nashto moha smritir labdha - my delusion is destroyed, my memory is restored. By Your grace, I stand firm with doubts dispelled. I shall do Your bidding. This is the complete transformation from chapter ones paralyzed, despairing warrior to a clarity-filled instrument ready for action. Smritir labdha - memory restored - refers to remembering his true nature, which ignorance had obscured.
Verses 74-75 shift to Sanjaya, the narrator, who expresses his own wonder: through Vyasas grace, I heard this secret yoga directly from Krishna, the Lord of Yoga. This acknowledges the lineage of transmission - from Krishna to Arjuna, witnessed by Sanjaya through Vyasas blessing. Knowledge flows through prepared channels, each receiving according to their capacity.
Arjunas transformation is available to each of us. The starting point - confusion, paralysis, conflicting duties - is universal. The path - listening with attention, receiving with faith, contemplating with discrimination - is accessible. The destination - nashto moha, smritir labdha - is the same: delusion destroyed, true nature remembered. Today, ask yourself: What delusion still clouds my understanding? What truth about myself have I forgotten? The Gita promises that with sustained engagement and grace, the clouds part. Gata-sandeha karishye vachanam tava - doubt-free, I shall act according to truth. This is the goal: not escape from action but action rooted in clarity.
